name: Bent-over dumbbell row
summary: Hinged forward with a flat back, row the dumbbells to the hips with the elbows driving back.
setup: Stand side-on to the phone, dumbbells hanging, hinge until the trunk is about 45° with the back flat. Row the weights to the hips, elbows brushing the ribs, then lower under control without standing up.
brief: Stand with the dumbbells hanging and hinge until the trunk is about 45 degrees, back flat. Row the weights to the hips, elbows brushing the ribs, then lower under control.
why: From the side the elbow angle gives each row, and the trunk rising with the weight — the way people cheat — shows as the shoulder–hip line lifting.
tempo: Up 1 s, squeeze 1 s, down 2 s.
regression: One arm with the other hand on a bench.
contraindications: Lower back pain in the hinge.

faults.label: Standing up with the weight
faults.tip: The trunk holds still; if it rises, the weight is too heavy.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Back rounding
faults.tip: Brace and keep the chest proud; lower the weight if it rounds.

faults.label: Standing up as you pull
faults.tip: Rising with each rep turns the row into a shrug and loads the lower back.

faults.label: Shrugging at the top
faults.tip: Pull the elbow past the ribs with the shoulder blade drawing down and in.

guide.cannotSee: The back rounding under a shirt.

points.t: Elbows drive back to the hips.
